informal.PackingBounds.FullMain.exact_binary_expo: The base-two logarithm of the unrestricted linear-program bound, divided by dimension, converges to -1/2 log_2(2 pi / e).
informal.PackingBounds.PackingBridge.sphere_packi: There is a vanishing error sequence such that, in every positive dimension, sphere-packing density is at most (sqrt(e / (2 pi)) plus that error) to the dimension.
informal.PackingBounds.sharpFullCohnElkiesManuscr: Packages the complete sharp asymptotic conclusions for the unrestricted program, including quotient-root, natural-logarithmic, and base-two limits, vanishing-error formulas, a universal bound for all admissible functions, and a certified decimal exponent interval.

records.title: Stafford 3.8
records.abstract: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.

informal.Stafford38.universalStatement: For every characteristic-zero field, every Weyl algebra rank, and every nonzero d, there are F, R, S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S.
informal.Stafford38.universalFixedSourceStatement: The stated fixed-source strengthening holds with its exact Bernstein-degree bound.

records.title: Verified Stallings folding for finitely generated subgroups of F2
records.abstract: Constructs a finite inverse automaton recognizing the subgroup generated by any finite list of signed words in the rank-two free group. Proves exact subgroup preservation and correctness of canonical reduced-word membership testing. Reusable infrastructure includes inverse-automaton walks, reduction-compatible traversal, finite fold congruences, coset potentials, flower graphs, and basis roses. Folding uses exhaustive finite search over Boolean relations; no complexity bound, core pruning, subgroup basis, intersection, or index algorithm is claimed.

informal.Stallings.folded_recognizer_exists: For every finite list S of signed words on two generators, there exist a finite type of states, a base state, and a partial transition table with inverse-labelled reverse edges, such that traversing the canonical reduced word of any g in FreeGroup (Fin 2) returns to the base exactly when g lies in the subgroup generated by the word values in S. The witness is the computed flower-graph fold.
informal.Stallings.foldWords_loopSubgroup_eq_gene: For every finite input list of signed words in the rank-two free group, the based-loop subgroup of the computed folded flower graph equals the subgroup generated by the input words.
informal.Stallings.foldedMembershipTest_eq_true_i: For any finite generating list S and any rank-two free-group element g, the executable folded-automaton test returns true if and only if g belongs to the subgroup generated by S. There is no efficiency guarantee for constructing the automaton.

records.title: Monotonicity Formula for Stationary Harmonic Maps
records.abstract: Formalizes the monotonicity formula for stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` maps with Euclidean target. The proof is target independent: it uses only the displayed weak gradient and a vanishing domain first variation, so no target-manifold structure enters the argument. From a bundled stationary Sobolev witness `StationaryW12LocMap u Omega` it proves, for `0 < s <= r < R0`, that the normalized energy `Theta(Du, a, rho) = rho^(2-n) * integral over B(a, rho) of |Du|^2` is monotone: `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r`, together with the exact increment formula `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r`. The Sobolev layer is project-defined from Mathlib's `MemLp`, weak-derivative identities, Bochner integration, and Euclidean measure theory, following the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser engineering choice; the internal proof routes through a radial vector-field first variation, a coarea/Radon-Nikodym radius representation, smooth radial cutoffs, and an absolute-continuity boundary step.

informal.LeanStationaryHarmonicMaps.StationaryHar: The public input package: a domain-variation stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` Sobolev map bundling a chosen weak gradient (`W12LocMapWitness`) with the vanishing domain first-variation identity. This is the object users construct to invoke the monotonicity theorem.

Witness-style monotonicity: from a stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` map package, the normalized weak energy `weakTheta` is monotone in the radius, `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r` for `0 < s <= r < R0`.

Witness-style monotonicity formula: the increment of `weakTheta` equals the nonnegative annular radial-energy term, `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r` for `0 < s < r < R0`.

Componentwise convenience wrapper: the same monotonicity inequality stated directly from the local `L^2`, measurability, weak-gradient, and first-variation hypotheses, without first constructing the witness package.

records.title: Split, cograph and threshold graph structures
records.abstract: Connects split partitions, cotrees and threshold creation sequences on Mathlib SimpleGraph. Proves the finite forbidden-induced-subgraph characterizations, split iff chordal and co-chordal, and completeness of cotrees and creation sequences. Supplies certificate-preserving operations, twins and nonempty union/join decompositions for cographs, maximum-clique split partitions, and induced/isomorphic transport of existing chordal elimination orders and clique trees. Classical graph theory is formalized; no new mathematical theorem, canonical certificate or recognition-time bound is claimed.

informal.SimpleGraph.isSplit_iff_forbidden_induce: A finite graph is split iff it contains no induced 2K2, C4 or C5.
informal.SimpleGraph.isSplit_iff_isChordal_and_co: A finite graph is split iff both it and its complement are chordal.
informal.SimpleGraph.isCograph_iff_nonempty_cotre: A finite graph is P4-free iff it is isomorphic to the graph of a cotree, whose constructors are empty, singleton, disjoint union and join.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_isSplit_and_: A graph has a split partition with nested independent-side neighbourhoods iff it is both split and P4-free. No finiteness is required.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_forbidden_in: A finite graph is threshold iff it contains no induced 2K2, C4 or P4.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_nonempty_cre: A finite graph is threshold iff it is isomorphic to a graph constructed from the empty graph by successively adding an isolated or universal vertex.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_twins: A finite cograph with at least two vertices has two distinct vertices with identical adjacency outside their pair, whether adjacent or not.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_union_root: A finite cograph that is not preconnected admits a cotree representation with a union root and two nonempty children. This is an existence claim, not a claim about every unreduced cotree.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_join_root: A preconnected finite cograph with at least two vertices admits a cotree representation with a join root and two nonempty children.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsSplit.exists_partition_wit: Every finite split graph admits a split partition whose clique part has maximum cardinality. Such a partition need not be unique.

records.title: The optimal exponent relating sumsets and difference sets
records.abstract: For a finite integer set A with at least two elements, proves that C(A) = log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly below 2, while explicit finite sets have exponents tending to 2. Thus 2 is the supremum and is never attained. Also gives an explicit witness within 10^(-999) of 2. This imports the upstream base-39 row-and-column variant, not the paper's base-12 automaton construction or its quantitative cardinality estimates. Supporting infrastructure includes injective digit expansions and the strict Pluennecke-Petridis equality argument for finite integer sets.

informal.SumDifferenceExponent.growthExponent_lt_: For every finite set A of integers with at least two elements, log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly less than 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.tendsto_growthExpo: The growth exponents of the explicit finite integer sets approximatingSet l converge to 2 as l tends to infinity; these sets have at least two elements whenever l is positive.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.isLUB_admissibleEx: The number 2 is the least upper bound of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.sSup_admissibleExp: The supremum of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements equals 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.supremum_not_attai: No finite integer set with at least two elements has growth exponent equal to 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.quantitative_examp: The explicitly defined finite integer set quantitativeSet has growth exponent strictly between 2 - 10^(-999) and 2.

records.title: Sums of Three Squares
records.abstract: Formalizes a blueprint step in the three-squares theorem using quadratic forms and geometry of numbers.

informal.LeanPool.SumsThreeSquares.blueprint_case: Proves the mod-8-equals-3 blueprint case for the three-squares theorem.

records.title: Sundog certificates
records.abstract: A referee-free, axiom-clean Lean development of coding-theory certificates: syndrome decoding soundness and lossiness bounds for GF(2) parity-check schemes (with a Reed–Solomon evaluation-dual variant), and a fully machine-checked correctness proof of the Karp reduction chain 3SAT ≤ 3DM ≤ X3C ≤ bounded-weight syndrome decoding. Only the logical iff of each reduction is formalized; polynomial-time bounds, NP classes, and Cook–Levin are unformalized external inputs, so NP-hardness of decoding is conditional on those standard facts.

informal.Sundog.SATReductionMain.sat_iff_decodes: The end-to-end reduction correctness: a formula is satisfiable iff its image under the composed 3SAT-to-decoding reduction is a yes-instance of bounded-weight syndrome decoding.
informal.Sundog.MatchingNPHard.threeDM_iff_X3C: The 3-dimensional matching instance has a perfect matching iff the reduced exact-cover-by-3-sets instance has an exact cover, both directions machine-checked.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.accept_sound: Soundness of the cheap syndrome-decoding verifier when it accepts: an exhibited light same-syndrome witness certifies the body is safe within the decoding radius.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.reject_sound: Soundness of the verifier when it rejects: a sound column-weight lower bound on the minimum same-syndrome weight rules out every light witness, so the body is genuinely unsafe.

records.title: Synthetic Euclidean geometry: Euclid's Elements Book I
records.abstract: Formalizes Book I of Euclid's Elements via an axiomatic synthetic-geometry system (incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area), culminating in the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.

informal.SyntheticEuclid4.IncidenceGeometry: The axiomatic class of synthetic Euclidean geometry, bundling points, lines, circles, and the incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area primitives with Euclid's axioms.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.square_of_len: Constructs a square on a given segment off a given line.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_construct: Constructs the three squares and parallelograms on the sides of a triangle used in the proof of the Pythagorean theorem.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras: Euclid I.47, the Pythagorean theorem, that the square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_converse: Euclid I.48, the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, that a triangle whose square areas satisfy the Pythagorean relation has a right angle.

records.title: The Three-Gap (Steinhaus) Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the three-gap (Steinhaus, three-distance) theorem: for every real `a` and every `N`, the `N`-point orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` partitions `[0,1)` into gaps taking at most three distinct lengths, and when exactly three occur the largest is the sum of the other two. The proof works in `[0,1)` via `Int.fract` (not `AddCircle`) through the two first-return times `η⁺` and `η⁻`, and is uniform in the rotation number, covering rational and irrational `a` with no case split.

informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_card_le_thre: For every real `a` and natural `N`, the gaps of the orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` take at most three distinct lengths.
informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_lengths_eq: When the gaps take exactly three distinct lengths, those lengths are precisely the two first returns `η⁺`, `η⁻`, and their sum `η⁺ + η⁻`; in particular the largest gap is the sum of the other two.

records.title: Turán's theorem (the "Book" weighting proof)
records.abstract: Formalizes the weighting/optimization proof of Turán's theorem from Proofs from THE BOOK, bounding the number of edges of a p-clique-free simple graph by (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n².

informal.Turan3.turans: Turán's theorem — a p-clique-free simple graph on n vertices has at most (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n² edges.
informal.Turan3.finale_bound: For any weight distribution on a p-clique-free graph, the total edge weight is at most ((p-1)(p-2)/2)·(1/(p-1))², the bound used to derive the edge count.
informal.Turan3.Better_forms_clique: Starting from any weight function, the minimal-support weight-non-decreasing improvement has support that forms a clique.
informal.Turan3.Enhance_total_weight_stricinc: Equalizing weights between a maximum- and minimum-weight vertex in the clique support strictly increases the total edge weight.

records.title: Tutte’s path theorem for matroids
records.abstract: Proves the modular-cut path theorem for finite matroids, with reusable rank-partition, hyperplane-separation, relative-complement, indecomposable-cover, and diamond constructions.

informal.TutteFormalization.path_theorem: In a finite connected matroid, any two hyperplanes containing a proper indecomposable flat and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a finite Tutte path all of whose vertices contain that flat and avoid the cut. Consecutive vertices are distinct hyperplanes with indecomposable corank-two intersection; repeated nonconsecutive vertices are permitted.
informal.TutteFormalization.path_theorem_of_indec: In any finite matroid, two hyperplanes containing an indecomposable flat F and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a Tutte path whose vertices contain F and avoid the cut. This strengthens the cited path theorem by requiring only connectedness of the contraction by F; properness of F follows from containment in an endpoint hyperplane.
informal.TutteFormalization.exists_indecomposable: If an indecomposable flat S and a flat U span the ground, every indecomposable flat T contained in both extends inside S to an indecomposable flat R spanning the ground with U, with corank R equal to rank U minus rank T.
informal.TutteFormalization.exists_relative_compl: For nested flats T contained in S, there is a flat U containing T whose intersection with S is T, whose join with S is the ground, and whose corank equals rank S minus rank T.

records.title: Ulm's theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups
records.abstract: Formalizes Ulm's classification theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups in arbitrary Lean universes. The development constructs the transfinite Ulm filtration and invariants, proves their invariance under additive equivalence, establishes Kaplansky's one-generator extension lemma, and completes the countable back-and-forth classification. A finite-group regression distinguishes Z/4 x Z/4 from Z/2 x Z/8 at the zeroth Ulm invariant.

informal.UlmsTheorem.ulm_theorem: For any prime p and any two countable reduced abelian p-groups in the same arbitrary Lean universe, the groups are additively isomorphic if and only if all of their classical Ulm invariants, indexed by universe-zero ordinals, agree.
informal.UlmsTheorem.iso_of_ulm_invariants: Equal Ulm invariants at every universe-zero ordinal imply an additive equivalence between countable reduced abelian p-groups, via finite height-preserving partial isomorphisms and a back-and-forth limit.
informal.UlmsTheorem.ulmInvariant_iso_invariant: An additive equivalence preserves every classical Ulm invariant.
informal.UlmsTheorem.UlmDifferentialRegression.no: The groups Z/4 x Z/4 and Z/2 x Z/8 are not additively isomorphic; the proof exercises the classification theorem and independently detects their different zeroth Ulm invariants.

records.title: Unconditional Schauder Bases
records.abstract: Develops an API for Schauder bases and unconditional Schauder bases of complete normed spaces, including ordered partial-sum convergence, rearrangement criteria for unconditionality, and an arbitrary-index variant built on unconditional summability, then proves a finite sign criterion: a family with dense closed span, nonzero vectors, and a uniform finite sign bound is the basis of an unconditional Schauder basis.

informal.UnconditionalCriterion.exists_unconditio: Finite sign criterion for sequences: if `x : ℕ → E` has dense closed linear span, every `x n` is nonzero, and finite sign changes are uniformly bounded by `C`, then `x` is the basis sequence of an unconditional Schauder basis.

Abstract-index form of the finite sign criterion: under the same dense span, nonzero, and uniform finite sign bound hypotheses for an arbitrarily indexed family, there is an abstractly indexed unconditional Schauder basis whose basis family is exactly `x`.

records.title: Virasoro Project
records.abstract: Formalizes the Virasoro algebra, its Witt-algebra central extension, Verma modules, and the basic bosonic Sugawara construction.

informal.VirasoroProject.VirasoroAlgebra: Defines the Virasoro algebra as a one-dimensional central extension of the Witt algebra.
informal.VirasoroProject.sugawaraRepresentation: Constructs the basic bosonic Sugawara representation of the Virasoro algebra from locally truncated Heisenberg actions.

records.title: Viscosity solutions, Aleksandrov differentiability and harmonic Dirichlet problems
records.abstract: Develops second-order semijets, smooth test-function equivalence, Jensen contact sets, convex Aleksandrov differentiability, the quadratic-penalty Ishii lemma and compact-domain comparison for degenerate elliptic equations. Perron assembly retains explicit comparison, barrier and bumping assumptions; these are discharged for classical harmonic Dirichlet existence on bounded open domains satisfying a uniform exterior sphere condition.

informal.AleksandrovDifferentiability.convexAleks: A convex real-valued function on an open subset of any finite-dimensional real inner product space is second-order differentiable at Lebesgue-almost every point.
informal.ViscositySolns.JensenContactSetPositiveM: Under the localized semiconvexity and strict-contact hypotheses, the contact set arising from sufficiently small linear perturbations has positive Lebesgue measure.
informal.ViscositySolns.QuadraticPenaltyIshiiLemm: For an upper semicontinuous function and a lower semicontinuous function on locally compact subsets of real coordinate space, doubled-variable maxima with the quadratic penalty yield closed semijets satisfying the Ishii block-matrix bounds.
informal.ViscositySolns.comparison_of_constantShi: A viscosity subsolution lies below a supersolution on a nonempty locally compact domain with compact closure, assuming boundary comparison, semicontinuity on the closure, properness, operator continuity, the Ishii structural condition and uniform scalar decrease.
informal.ViscositySolns.viscositySubsolution_iff_: On an open domain, semijet and smooth C² test-function formulations of viscosity subsolutions agree for Hessian-continuous, symmetric-part-invariant operators.
informal.ViscositySolns.dirichlet_harmonic_modulu: On a bounded open subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space with a uniform exterior sphere condition, Lipschitz data on its closure admit a continuous extension that agrees on the boundary and is C² and harmonic in the domain, with a boundary modulus depending only on the domain and Lipschitz constant.

records.title: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
records.abstract: Proves the maximum-degree-plus-one edge-colouring bound for finite simple graphs by fans and Kempe exchanges. A separate component-swapping argument equitably rebalances any finite proper edge colouring on its original palette. Together they give equitable proper edge colourings on any palette of at least maximum degree plus one colours, with every class bounded by the ceiling of the average class size. Extracted from the published Paper IV formalization; these are classical colouring results, not a claim to new mathematics or to the paper's clique-partition bound.

informal.LeanPool.Vizing.lineGraph_colorable: The line graph of a finite simple graph G is colourable with maximum degree of G plus one colours.
informal.SimpleGraph.lineGraph_chromaticNumber_le: The chromatic number of the line graph of a finite simple graph G is at most maximum degree of G plus one.
informal.LeanPool.Vizing.Equitable.exists_equitab: Every proper edge colouring of a finite simple graph with a finite palette admits a proper recolouring on the same palette in which any two colour classes differ in size by at most one.
informal.LeanPool.Vizing.exists_equitable_edge_co: For every finite simple graph G and natural c at least maximum degree of G plus one, there is an equitable proper edge colouring with c colours; each colour class has at most ceiling(|E(G)|/c) edges.

records.title: Mean-field derivation and well-posedness of the Vlasov equation
records.abstract: Formalizes the mean-field limit, Dobrushin stability, and forward-in-time well-posedness for the Vlasov equation via Wasserstein-1 optimal transport.

informal.Vlasov.vlasovWellPosedness: Forward-in-time existence of a Lagrangian solution to the Vlasov equation on any finite horizon, for interaction forces that are Lipschitz gradients of an even pair potential (class AssW) — with no smallness restriction on the Lipschitz constant.
informal.Vlasov.dobrushin: A Wasserstein-1 form of Dobrushin's 1979 stability estimate (the original uses a truncated metric) - two Lagrangian Vlasov solutions with finite first moments at every time separate at most at an exponential Gronwall rate.
informal.Vlasov.meanFieldLimit: Conditional mean-field limit - given Wasserstein-1 convergence of the initial empirical data and a uniform Dobrushin stability estimate for the empirical curves, the N-particle empirical measures converge to the Vlasov solution uniformly on any finite horizon.
informal.Vlasov.weak_isLagrangianVlasovSolutionOn: On a time window with L * T^2 < 1, a weak solution with the standing regularity (even C^2 pair potential AssW2, finite first moments, narrow continuity, time-continuity of the convolution force at each point, continuity of the convolution-derivative field, and a uniform spatial first-moment bound on the window) is Lagrangian - the pushforward of its initial datum along the characteristic flow.

records.title: The Wallace problem in ZFC
records.abstract: Formalizes in ZFC a Hausdorff countably compact group topology without nontrivial convergent sequences on every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum. It specializes the construction to the rational direct sum and the additive real group, and derives a commutative Tychonoff countably compact cancellative semigroup that is not a group.

informal.Wallace.torsionFreeAbelianGroup_mainTheo: Every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum admits a Hausdorff countably compact group topology with no nontrivial convergent sequences.
informal.Wallace.continuumRationalGroup_and_real_: Both the continuum-indexed rational direct sum and the additive group of real numbers admit such Hausdorff countably compact group topologies without nontrivial convergent sequences.
informal.Wallace.commutativeTychonoffWallaceCount: There exists a commutative Tychonoff countably compact topological semigroup with two-sided cancellation which is not a group.

records.title: Whitehead's theorem for CW-complexes
records.abstract: Formalizes Whitehead's theorem — a continuous map between CW-complexes that induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence — including the supporting theory of CW-complexes, relative homotopy groups, the homotopy extension property, and compression of maps.

informal.WhiteheadTheorem: Proves that a continuous map between CW-complexes inducing isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence.

records.title: Irrationality of the Riemann zeta function at five
records.abstract: Proves that Mathlib's Riemann zeta function at five is an irrational real number, following Aabir Fauzan's September 2026 preprint. Constructs integer polynomials of degree 37n with positive values at zeta(5) that decay exponentially in n squared. Includes a general integer-polynomial irrationality criterion, Hankel determinant and moment-integral identities, logarithmic-energy estimates, prime-adic integrality bounds, and kernel-checked rational certificates. The formalization uses a different normalizer and a positive decay constant in place of the paper's specific constant 139/5. Reuses the prime number theorem infrastructure already in the MooreBound project.

informal.Zeta5Irrational.irrational_five: There exists an irrational real number x whose complex coercion equals Mathlib's Riemann zeta function evaluated at five.
informal.Zeta5Irrational.main_estimate: There is a positive real c such that, for all sufficiently large n, an integer polynomial Q of degree 37n is a positive rational multiple of the constructed determinant polynomial and satisfies 0 < Q(zeta(5)) < exp(-c*n^2).
informal.Zeta5Irrational.irrational_of_eventually: A real xi is irrational if, eventually, integer polynomials of degree at most d(n) have positive values at xi bounded by epsilon(n), and b^d(n)*epsilon(n) tends to zero for every positive natural b.

records.title: Thakur's hypotheses on power sums of F_q[t]
records.abstract: Formalizes four components of Thakur's hypotheses on power sums over finite polynomial rings, including uniqueness and monotonicity results for the carry-free digit optimization problems and the Laurent-series expansion of finite-field power sums.

informal.ZetaH123.H1.main_theorem: Proves uniqueness of the admissible base-q decomposition maximizing the H1 power-sum weight functional.
informal.ZetaH123.H2.main: Proves the H2 unique-minimizer statement for the recursive digit/carry-free optimization problem defining the values s_d(k).
informal.ZetaH123.H3.main_theorem: Proves the H3 monotonicity statement that s_d(k) is strictly less than s_d(k+1) when p does not divide k.
informal.ZetaH123.Lem41.main: Proves the Lemma 4.1 Laurent-series expansion for S_d(k), with nonzero coefficients indexed by the carry-free tuples.

records.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function
records.abstract: Formalizes Lamzouri's Hilbert-space proof of lower bounds for simple and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta function. From explicit Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation hypotheses, the development proves that eventually more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line and more than 83.625% are distinct. It includes the finite-multiset Hilbert-space inequality, zeta-zero multiplicity symmetries, an admissible cutoff construction, and certified trigonometric estimates.

informal.ZetaZeros.simple_proportion_d4: Assuming the stated Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation formulas, beyond some height more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and lie on the critical line.
informal.ZetaZeros.distinct_proportion_d5: Under the same two explicit analytic hypotheses, beyond some height more than 83.625% of nontrivial zeta zeros are distinct.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_simpleRealPart_lower: Bounds from below the number of multiplicity-one real points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the squared test-kernel sum of any admissible function.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_lower: Bounds from below the number of distinct points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the same Hilbert-space kernel method.

records.title: Linear independence of 1, zeta(2), and zeta(3)
records.abstract: Proves that 1, the Riemann zeta function at 2, and its value at 3 are linearly independent over the rationals, using integer polynomial approximation, p-adic coefficient bounds, prime-edge nonvanishing, and logarithmic potential energy estimates for Hankel determinants. Includes reusable irrationality criteria, contour integration, Andreief identities, Newton-basis valuation bounds, and energy inequalities for finite measures. The cited source is the completed Lean proof; independent novelty of the informal argument is not claimed.

informal.Zeta32.one_zeta_two_zeta_three_linearInd: The three complex numbers 1, riemannZeta 2, and riemannZeta 3 are linearly independent over the rational numbers.
informal.Zeta32Acceptance.one_zeta_two_zeta_three: For rational a, b, and c, if a plus b times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^2 plus c times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^3 is zero, then all three coefficients are zero; both sums range over natural numbers k.
informal.Zeta32.zeta3_sub_rat_mul_zeta2_irrationa: For every rational r, the real series for zeta(3) minus r times the real series for zeta(2) is irrational.

records.title: Irrationality of ζ(3)
records.abstract: Formalizes Beukers' proof of Apéry's theorem for ζ(3), including the integral identities, denominator estimates, positivity, upper bounds, and final irrationality contradiction.

informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.linear_int: Clears denominators in the Apéry integral to produce a linear form in 1 and ζ(3).
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_pos: Proves positivity of the transformed Beukers-Apéry integral.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_upper: Bounds the Beukers-Apéry integral by a geometric factor times the ζ(3) series.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.fun1_tendsto_ze: Shows that the denominator-cleared Apéry linear forms tend to zero.

records.title: ZFLean
records.abstract: Develops a practical ZFC set-theory framework with von Neumann naturals, integers, rationals, functions, embeddings, isomorphisms, booleans, and sums.

informal.ZFSet.isIso_of_biembedding: Proves a Cantor-Bernstein theorem for ZF sets.
informal.ZFSet.ZFNat.induction: Provides induction for the von Neumann natural numbers.
informal.ZFSet.ZFInt.induction: Provides induction for the quotient construction of ZF integers.

records.title: The Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon information inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the Zhang-Yeung inequality, the first known non-Shannon-type entropy inequality, together with its dual and averaged forms derived through the copy lemma.

informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung: Proves the Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon-type information inequality for four discrete random variables.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_dual: Proves the dual form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_averaged: Proves the averaged symmetric form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.

records.title: The Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem on equitable colourings
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem (1970), conjectured by Erdős in 1964: every finite graph with maximum degree at most r has an equitable proper colouring with r + 1 colours, i.e. a proper colouring whose colour classes differ in size by at most one. The exact form is also proved: if the number of vertices is s(r + 1), every colour class has exactly s vertices (the colouring form of Erdős Problem #914). Version 2 adds the form with any number k > Δ(G) of colours (Mathlib's SimpleGraph.maxDegree), deduced from the theorem with r = k − 1. The proof follows the short argument of Kierstead and Kostochka (2008): induction on the number of edges; after deleting an edge, a nearly equitable colouring is repaired by moving vertices along paths of an auxiliary digraph on the colour classes (Lemma 2.1); when the large class is inaccessible, a family of terminal classes, solo edges and a discharging count with weights q/|S_z| (Lemmas 2.2–2.3) produce a recolouring that either finishes the colouring or strictly increases the number of accessible classes, using the induction hypothesis on the inaccessible part. The general case is reduced to the divisible one by adding a disjoint complete graph.

records.title: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Vizing's theorem: every finite simple graph G has a proper edge colouring with Δ(G) + 1 colours, stated with Mathlib's line graph (G.lineGraph is (Δ(G) + 1)-colourable, hence χ'(G) ≤ Δ(G) + 1), proved with fans and Kempe chain exchanges. It also proves the equitable refinement: for every c ≥ Δ(G) + 1 there is a proper edge colouring with colours Fin c in which any two colour classes (including unused colours) differ in size by at most one (McDiarmid 1972), obtained by balancing a Vizing colouring with alternating-component moves that strictly decrease a square energy. Version 2 adds the lower bound Δ(G) ≤ χ'(G) (the edges at a vertex of maximum degree form a clique of the line graph) and hence the dichotomy χ'(G) ∈ {Δ(G), Δ(G) + 1} (class 1 / class 2).

records.title: Near-regular hypergraph matchings and the asymptotic triangle-packing gap
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of four results. (1) A finite nibble theorem: r-uniform hypergraphs whose degrees are at most (1+μ)d everywhere and at least (1−μ)d outside an exceptional set of at most η|V| vertices, with codegrees at most μd, have matchings with at least (1−β)|V|/r edges. (2) The fractional–integral triangle-packing gap is o(n²) uniformly over finite graphs: every large graph has an edge-disjoint triangle family P such that every fractional triangle packing has weight at most |P| + εn² (the triangle case of Haxell–Rödl). (3) The cover form: a fractional triangle cover of weight at most |P| + εn² exists. (4) Version 2, the transfer form used in decomposition theory: every large graph on n vertices that has a fractional triangle decomposition has an edge-disjoint triangle family covering all but at most ηn² edges; it follows from (2), since a fractional decomposition is a fractional packing of weight e(G)/3 and a packing P covers exactly 3|P| edges. The proof of (1)–(3) combines a nibble with second-moment and Freedman-type concentration, a low-degree core reduction, Mathlib's Szemerédi regularity lemma with a cluster linear program rounded by explicit designs, and LP duality.

records.title: Graphs of large girth and large chromatic number: Erdős, Mycielski, and the fractional chromatic number of Mycielski graphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three classical results on graphs with large chromatic number. (1) Erdős' 1959 theorem: for every g and k there is a finite graph with girth greater than g and chromatic number greater than k, in the structural form given by the probabilistic argument (for every ε > 0 and all large n, a graph on n vertices with girth greater than g whose independent sets have fewer than εn vertices). (2) Mycielski's 1955 construction M(G): it preserves and reflects triangle-freeness, M(G) is (k+1)-colourable exactly when G is k-colourable, χ(M(G)) = χ(G) + 1 for every finite G, and iterating from K₂ gives triangle-free graphs with 3·2ⁿ − 1 vertices and chromatic number n + 2. (3) Larsen, Propp and Ullman (1995): for the fractional chromatic number χ_f (least total weight of a fractional colouring by independent sets), χ_f(M(G)) = χ_f(G) + 1/χ_f(G) for every finite graph G with at least one vertex. Version 2 adds (2) and (3); the statements of version 1 are unchanged. Mathlib has girth and chromatic number but none of these theorems, and no fractional chromatic number.

records.title: First Betti numbers of five-generated numerical semigroups
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization project for (F) an explicit two-parameter family of minimally five-generated numerical semigroups <m, m+1, m+k, m+2k-1, m+2k>, m = 2kq+1, whose toric ideal has spanRank exactly 4k+2. Planned scope for (W), a proposed finite-width bound beta1 <= 2w+2 (4 <= w <= 40), not all formalized: the generic fiber-graph infrastructure, both algebraic bridges (only the upper bridge is formalized; the reverse bridge is not), the corrected singleton-counting decomposition beta1 + p = 5 + N, the pair-component antichain lemma and certificate-checker soundness (not yet written). Version 1 targets F; W is stated and excluded from the release comparator. F is sorry-free at 793e759.

records.title: Galvin's theorem for bipartite multigraphs, the Dinitz problem and stable matchings
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Galvin’s theorem for finite bipartite multigraphs: every assignment of finite edge lists of size at least the maximum incidence degree admits a proper edge coloring, with parallel edges counted separately. It includes ordinary edge coloring with Δ colors and the matching lower bound, and the Borodin–Kostochka–Woodall theorem for local lists (lists of size at least the larger degree of the two ends of each edge suffice). The previously registered simple-graph Galvin theorem, Dinitz problem and Gale–Shapley stable matching theorem are retained.

records.title: Counting Steiner triple systems: Wilson (1974) and Linial–Luria (2013)
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of R. M. Wilson's "Nonisomorphic Steiner triple systems" (inequality (2.1), Theorems 1–4, Lemmas 3–5, including the exact numbers of Latin squares of orders 6, 7 and 8 and the bounds N(19) ≥ 2450, N(21) ≥ 2160980, N(25) ≥ 163929929318400) and of N. Linial and Z. Luria's "An upper bound on the number of Steiner triple systems" (Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 with explicit error terms). Version 2 adds a proof of the van der Waerden permanent theorem (Egorychev, Falikman), following Gurvits's proof as simplified by Laurent and Schrijver. The parts of Wilson's Theorems 2 and 3 that rely on it are stated both as implications from the hypothesis vdWPC, as in the paper, and unconditionally (theorem2_full, theorem3_full). Finite computations are kernel-checked certificates (no native_decide). Mathlib does not contain these results.

records.title: Sums of primes, after Hardy and Littlewood 1923, Partitio Numerorum III, Theorems B to F proved without Hypothesis R, and Theorem A on Hypothesis R for 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4
records.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no hypothesis, of Theorems B, C, D, E and F of G. H. Hardy and J. E. Littlewood, Some problems of Partitio Numerorum III, Acta Math. 44, 1923. Hardy and Littlewood proved these theorems on their Hypothesis R, a form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions; here they are proved unconditionally, from Vinogradov's estimate for exponential sums over primes and the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, so the argument is not Hardy and Littlewood's own for Theorems B, D and E. Formalized: Theorem B, the asymptotic for the weighted count nu_r of n as an ordered sum of r primes, for every r at least 3 and n of the parity of r, with the singular series written as the paper's product over the odd primes dividing n, and nu_r of n is o of n^{r-1} for unlike parity; Theorem C, N_r of n is asymptotic to nu_r of n over log^r n; Theorem D, the ternary asymptotic with the constant C_3 and every large odd number a sum of three odd primes; Theorem E, the asymptotic for four odd primes, every large even number a sum of four odd primes, one of which may be assigned; and Theorem F, that an asymptotic of Conjecture A's shape for binary Goldbach can only carry the constant 2 C_2, together with a check that the printed formula 4.23 has a misprint. Version 2 adds Theorem A, eq 3.113: for every r at least 3 and every Theta with 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4, on the paper's own Hypothesis R at level Theta, that no Dirichlet L-function has a zero with real part above Theta, nu_r of n equals the singular series S_r of n of 3.114 times n^{r-1} over the factorial of r minus 1, plus O of n^{r-1+Theta-3/4} times a power of log n, for all n from some n0. The paper allows every Theta below 3/4; the Lean statement covers only 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4. The entry also proves derived results on Theorem A that are not statements of the paper: its hypotheses other than the zero-free one hold together, GRH gives the zero-free hypothesis for every Theta at least 1/2, Theorem A at Theta equal to 47/64 on GRH, and S_r of n is positive with a summable series in like parity. Ternary Goldbach is Helfgott's theorem; binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent; the statements were written from the paper's page images by AI agents and are offered for human audit.

records.title: Helling's theorem: the maximal subgroups of SL₂(ℝ) commensurable with SL₂(ℤ)
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of Helling's theorem and of consequences for normalizers. A subgroup G ≤ SL₂(ℝ) is commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) if G ∩ SL₂(ℤ) has finite index in G and in SL₂(ℤ); Γ₀(N)⁺ is the group generated by the Atkin–Lehner elements of level N, and contains Γ₀(N). Every G commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) is conjugate into Γ₀(N)⁺ for some squarefree N, by (det A)^{−1/2}·A for an integral matrix A with det A > 0. For every N ≥ 1, Γ₀(N)⁺ is commensurable with SL₂(ℤ), and for squarefree N it is maximal among such groups; so the maximal subgroups of SL₂(ℝ) commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) are the conjugates of the Γ₀(N)⁺, N squarefree, that are commensurable with SL₂(ℤ) (Duncan's Theorem 2.11, in SL₂(ℝ)), and Γ₀(4)⁺ is not maximal. The commensurator of SL₂(ℤ) in SL₂(ℝ) consists of the (det A)^{−1/2}·A. For every Γ commensurable with SL₂(ℤ), the normalizer of Γ in SL₂(ℝ) is commensurable with SL₂(ℤ), so Nor(Γ)/Γ is finite, and Nor(Γ) is conjugate into Γ₀(N)⁺ for some squarefree N. The proof is the argument with p-adic trees that Duncan attributes to Conway, with an integral matrix for each vertex and distances computed from p-adic valuations of determinants and of the gcd of the entries; the vertices and edges fixed at the different primes are glued with the Smith normal form. 9 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Continuous open images of Polish spaces
records.abstract: Continuous open surjections preserve the strong Choquet property in arbitrary topological spaces. An explicit full-history strategy lifts each legal target play coherently, keeps the marked point, and maps an actual common source point. Consequently a continuous open metrizable image of a Polish space is Polish. A second-countable completely metrizable source gives a completely metrizable metrizable image. A regular Hausdorff codomain also suffices, by inherited second countability and Urysohn metrizability. These are classical results; no novelty or priority is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The expander mixing lemma and the Alon–Boppana bound
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two basic results of spectral graph theory, stated through the adjacency quadratic form on vectors orthogonal to the all-ones vector: the expander mixing lemma of Alon and Chung (for a d-regular graph on n ≥ 2 vertices with |x·Ax| ≤ μ‖x‖² on 𝟙⊥, |e(S,T) − d|S||T|/n| ≤ μ√(|S||T|)), and the Alon–Boppana bound in Nilli's form (a d-regular graph, d ≥ 2, with two vertices at distance at least 2k + 4 has a nonzero x ⟂ 𝟙 with x·Ax ≥ (2√(d−1) − (2√(d−1) − 1)/(k+1))‖x‖²). Mathlib has adjacency matrices but neither result.

records.title: Cubic-rate irrationality for reciprocal sums
records.abstract: Every positive strictly increasing zero-indexed integer sequence a with n^3(a_n^2/a_(n+1) - 1 - 3/n) tending to zero has an irrational reciprocal sum. The entry also states the exact integer-tail and number-field steps used to exclude the resulting cubic profile: positive-density exceptions, primitive gcd reduction, square specialisation, scale twelve, forbidden words modulo seven, and regular-rate extraction. The printed one-indexed paper theorem uses its stated finite-prefix argument. The separate bounded-increment Sylvester criterion in the paper is outside this configuration, and the unrestricted Erdős problem #243 remains open. The selected Challenge explicitly retains the strict monotonicity and positivity of a, the HasSum witness for its reciprocal series, and the n³-scaled rate limit. It does not silently infer that rate from the weaker condition a_(n+1)/a_n² → 1.

records.title: Uniform sparse rationalisation of dyadic series
records.abstract: Given any convergent dyadic series with nonnegative integer coefficients, any finite prefix and any eventually unbounded correction allowance, one common permitted set of upper Banach density zero supports nonnegative integer corrections realising every target in a nondegenerate interval above the original sum. Each fixed modulus eventually divides both corrections and cumulative corrections beyond a cutoff independent of the target. With polylogarithmic allowance, the selected theorem also bounds support in dyadic windows and preserves empirical block distributions in total variation for lengths o(log log X), uniformly in the target. The entry additionally states exact prime-to-gap summation identities and tail rationality criteria. It does not select the prime-gap joint countermodel, which in the paper uses named outside inputs, and makes no claim that corrected cumulative positions are prime or that the original prime series is irrational.

records.title: Infinite rank of the three-prime running-LCM kernel
records.abstract: For pairwise distinct primes p, q and r, the three-prime reciprocal running-LCM kernel has nonzero square minors of every order, with row and column indices chosen independently of the third exponent. Consequently it admits no finite rational separated representation. The selected entry also proves an exact rank formula for threshold-column matrices, an explicit two-by-two example at 2,3,5, separation in the two-prime comparison, and the four-base dyadic recurrence for the actual 2,3,5 sum. A uniform finite-rank approximation statement concerns the rescaled carry matrix. The stronger unit-determinant modular minors are in E269_08 and are outside this configuration. Infinite kernel rank does not prove irrationality of the running-LCM series. In the selected rank theorem the determinants remain nonzero for every fixed third exponent k using the same injective row and column maps. The distance theorem concerns a rescaled real carry matrix and is not an approximation lower bound for the original summable kernel.

records.title: An explicit rational-base irrationality region for Zudilin's Lambert series
records.abstract: For coprime integers a > b >= 1 satisfying b^μ < a, equivalently log b / log a < θ*, the selected Lean theorems prove irrationality of F(a/b). They include the base 31/4 and every positive integer power, plus associated irrationality-measure bounds. The region excludes 3/2. This configuration does not select the paper's later sharp fixed-base asymptotic or all-rank Hankel results.

records.title: Carry and divisor-channel criteria for the factorial-minus-one reciprocal series
records.abstract: For the reciprocal series with denominators n! - 1, the selected Lean theorems give an exact carry characterization of rationality, divisor-channel coordinates, and a finite gcd moment certificate. Companion-orbit and complementary tail criteria are included with their stated hypotheses. These structural results do not certify the paper's large computed denominator exclusions or resolve the irrationality question.

records.title: Open Baire-space representation of Polish spaces
records.abstract: Every nonempty Polish space is the image of Baire space, the product of countably many discrete natural-number spaces, under a continuous open surjection. The proof constructs a countably branching nonempty open scheme with nested closures, covering children and geometrically shrinking diameters. The image of each basic cylinder is proved exactly equal to its scheme open set. This yields openness and surjectivity of the limit map; existence is also characterized by nonemptiness. These are classical results, with no novelty or priority claim.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Alexandrov–Urysohn characterization of Baire space
records.abstract: A topological space is homeomorphic to Baire space, the countable product of discrete natural numbers, if and only if it is nonempty, Polish, has a basis of clopen sets, and every compact subset has empty interior. The construction partitions each nonempty clopen set into countably infinitely many distinct nonempty clopen children with arbitrarily small diameter. A fully branching shrinking scheme gives a continuous open bijective limit map and therefore a homeomorphism. The converse uses finite coordinate images of compact Baire subsets. This formalizes a classical theorem of Alexandrov and Urysohn; no novelty or priority claim is made.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The Bondy–Simonovits even cycle theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Bondy–Simonovits theorem: for every k ≥ 2 there is a constant C such that every finite simple graph on n vertices with no cycle of length exactly 2k has at most C·n^(1+1/k) edges, i.e. ex(n, C_2k) = O(n^(1+1/k)). The statement is existential in C (the proof gives C = 16k + 4); the sharper constants of later work and the full range of even cycle lengths in Bondy–Simonovits's paper are not stated. Mathlib has walks and cycles but not this theorem.

records.title: Brouwer characterization of Cantor space
records.abstract: A topological space is homeomorphic to Cantor space, the countable product of discrete Boolean spaces, if and only if it is nonempty, compact, metrizable, has a basis of clopen sets, and has no isolated points. A full binary clopen scheme decides an enumerated basis one element at each depth. Its point-address map is continuous; compact nested intersections realize every binary branch, and basis decisions separate points. A continuous bijection from a compact space to the Hausdorff Cantor space is a homeomorphism. This formalizes a classical theorem of Brouwer; no mathematical novelty or priority claim is made.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Nivat's conjecture
records.abstract: For every configuration on the integer plane over an arbitrary finite alphabet, a positive k by n rectangle with at most k*n occurring translated patterns forces a nonzero global period of the original configuration. The statement includes equality at the complexity threshold and rectangles of width or height one. The Lean proof is due to Catenation, my custom agentic framework, translating the argument in my paper into Lean. The proof uses Laurent annihilators, a sharp periodic-wedge complexity bound, generating polygons, and selection of the same nonperiodic orbit point throughout the periodic-background construction. Its mathematical setting is multidimensional symbolic dynamics and combinatorics of low-complexity configurations. The independent Challenge states the full conjecture using only standard Mathlib notions.

records.title: Sierpiński's characterization of the rationals
records.abstract: Every nonempty countable metrizable topological space without isolated points is homeomorphic to the rational numbers with their usual topology. Conversely, these four properties characterize spaces homeomorphic to the rationals. A clopen basis is derived from the hypotheses. Scheduled binary clopen splits give each point an address with both bits arbitrarily far out; the induced lexicographic order is proved dense, without endpoints, and to generate exactly the original topology. The countable dense-order isomorphism theorem then gives the homeomorphism. This formalizes classical mathematics; no mathematical novelty or priority claim is made.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Multiplicative bases and standardness of representation-finite algebras
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of two classical theorems of Bautista, Gabriel, Roiter and Salmerón on finite-dimensional representation-finite algebras over an algebraically closed field. Theorem A: every such algebra, in any characteristic, has a normed multiplicative basis, that is, a basis containing a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents, closed under products up to zero, and meeting every power of the Jacobson radical in a basis of that power. Theorem B: every basic such algebra over a field of characteristic different from two is standard, that is, its category of indecomposable modules is equivalent to the mesh category of its Auslander–Reiten quiver by an equivalence sending each vertex to its module. The proof follows the deformation-theoretic approach of the formalized manuscript: the standard form is the graded algebra of the radical filtration of the category of indecomposable modules, and the original algebra is recovered as a filtered deformation of it. The Auslander–Reiten theory used is proved in the library.

records.title: Stability of planar fronts in reaction-diffusion systems
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of effective dynamics near spectrally stable planar fronts in reaction-diffusion systems under small, bounded uniformly continuous perturbations. The main result constructs global solutions and approximates the perturbed front by a phase evolving according to a viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equation, with a uniform quantitative error bound.

records.title: The Graham–Pollak theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Graham–Pollak theorem: the edge set of the complete graph K_n cannot be partitioned into fewer than n − 1 complete bipartite graphs, together with the matching construction by n − 1 stars. Biclique decompositions are encoded by families of pairs of disjoint vertex sets covering every pair of distinct vertices exactly once. Mathlib does not contain this theorem.

records.title: Fifth dimension subgroups: D₅ = γ₅ when G/γ₂ is finite of exponent 3, candidates for a counterexample, and a reduction of Kourovka 20.84
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying S. Vorobev, "On the inclusion D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G): reductions, the Lie-ring proof, and evidence" (preprint, 2026; submitted to arXiv math.GR on 2026-10-22). The integral dimension subgroups D_n(G) = {g ∈ G : g − 1 ∈ Δ(G)^n} are defined from the augmentation ideal of Mathlib's integral group ring. Kourovka Problem 20.84 asks whether D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G) for every group; it is open and is not claimed here. Unconditional results: D_5(G) = γ_5(G) whenever G/γ_2(G) is finite of exponent 3, and more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group whose cubes form a cyclic group (paper, Theorems 6.6 and 6.8; the inclusion part of Tahara's 1981 description of D_5 is formalized for this); D_5(G) lies in the Jennings product M_5(G) for finite 2-groups of class at most 3; and, for "candidates" (the paper's minimal-counterexample shape among finite 2-groups of class 3), there is no candidate of order 2^11 with Q/P_3 ≅ Z/4 × (Z/2)^7 and none of order 2^11 and rank at least 8 (paper, Lemma 5.6 and Proposition 5.7). Conditional results, with every assumption an explicit hypothesis: the reduction of Problem 20.84 to finite 2-groups of class exactly 3 assuming D_3 = γ_3, Passi's D_4^2 ⊆ γ_4 and Gruenberg's residual theorem (Proposition 2.1); a minimal counterexample is a candidate assuming D_3 = γ_3 (Lemma 5.2); and D_5 = 1 for groups of order 2^11, class at most 3 and rank at least 8, assuming D_3 = γ_3 and the paper's computer result for order 2^10 (Proposition 5.7, D_5 form).

records.title: Control flow obfuscation with irreducible loops and self-modifying code
records.abstract: Lean 4 development (no Mathlib) of the mathematics, algorithms and security statements of Morse, Alqaradaghi and Kozsik, "Control flow obfuscation with irreducible loops and self-modifying code": a self-modifying-code solver for 2-SAT and the planted instance generator as an algorithm, the extremal numbers of irreducible loops and multiple-entry edges (the families Kn and Mn), the irreducible-loop transformations of Figures 5 and 6, the Boolean control-flow graphs of AES, and the security statements of Section 5.1 relative to an explicit structural threat model. Two Challenges are submitted from one development: Challenge.lean (solver, extremal numbers, transformations, security model) and ChallengeAES.lean (the AES graphs); a Challenge may have at most 1,000 lines.

records.title: Temporal cliques admit spanners of size O(n log n)
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with O(n log n) edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result is due to Casteigts, Peters and Schoeters (ICALP 2019, JCSS 2021); the formal proof follows the dismountability-only proof of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025, §§2–4), which reduces cliques to bi-cliques and concludes with the one-sided dismountability of Angrick et al. (ESA 2024). The compared statements give an explicit bound of 2n⌈log₂ n⌉ + 4n edges and the asymptotic O(n log n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen.

records.title: Log-square quadrupolar correlation decay in two-dimensional RP2 and RP3 models
records.abstract: For the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor RP2 and RP3 director models, the absolute quadrupolar two-point correlation is bounded by C exp(-c (log(2+r))^2) at every finite bound on the dimensionless coupling. The positive constants are uniform over finite square-lattice subgraphs, arbitrary signed edge couplings within that bound, and observation sites; r is the integer lattice infinity distance. The compared statements use explicit normalized spherical product measures and Gibbs-integral quotients, with observable (n_x dot n_y)^2 - 1/3 or - 1/4, respectively. No response estimate or decay certificate is assumed. This registry interface selects the two finite-volume bounds. It does not assert exponential decay at all temperatures or the absence of every thermodynamic or topological transition. The larger development also contains local-limit and high-temperature results, which are not selected by this Comparator entry.

records.title: Almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the theorem that almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum, which is Haemers' conjecture for the generalized spectrum. The generalized spectrum of a graph is the spectrum of its adjacency matrix A together with the spectrum of the adjacency matrix J - I - A of its complement, and a graph is determined by its generalized spectrum (DGS) if every graph with the same generalized spectrum is isomorphic to it. The main theorem, DGSMain.almost_all_graphs_are_DGS, states that the proportion of the graphs on the vertex set {0, ..., n-1} that are DGS tends to 1 as n tends to infinity; that is, the random graph G(n, 1/2) is DGS with probability tending to one. This is Theorem 1.1 of the accompanying paper, and the formalization contains its whole proof: the reduction to local failures at primes through the rational orthogonal matrices relating generalized cospectral graphs, Seidel switching, Fourier analysis of random symmetric matrices over finite rings, inverse Littlewood-Offord estimates over finite fields, rank estimates for random symmetric matrices modulo primes, and the exclusion of rational factors of the characteristic polynomial of a random symmetric sign matrix with zero diagonal. The results that the paper quotes from the literature are also proved: Kneser's addition theorem, the theorem of Johnson and Newman on generalized cospectral graphs, and the cases used of the theorems of Tao and Vu (a random symmetric sign matrix has simple spectrum) and of O'Rourke and Touri (G(n, 1/2) is controllable), the last two by a new argument based on the methods of the paper. The proof uses only the standard axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice.

records.title: The Euclidean algorithm is not optimal among uniform processes
records.abstract: For every pair a ≥ b ≥ 1 there is a straight-line derivation of gcd(a, b) that uses only the remainder operation on available values and makes at most (3 + o(1)) log₂ a / log₂ log₂ a remainder calls, uniformly in b ≤ a; Euclid's algorithm needs about 1.44 log₂ a calls in the worst case. The proof stores a prefix of the Euclidean remainder sequence, shows that modulo every sufficiently large modulus at most three of its values share a residue class, and uses close residues to shrink the modulus by three remainder calls at a time. Consequently the intrinsic calls(rem)-complexities of the gcd and of coprimeness, in the sense of Moschovakis's Abstract Recursion and Intrinsic Complexity, are O(log a / log log a). This refutes Conjecture 3.4 of Moschovakis's 2012 notes "Absolute lower bounds for uniform processes" and the version (4F-5) of the Main Conjecture in the book, both for the structure (ℕ, rem, eq0) and for Nε = (ℕ, rem, eq0, eq1). The same bound answers negatively the closure-depth question of van den Dries and Moschovakis (2009): there are no positive integers aₙ → ∞, bₙ and C > 0 whose closure depth g(aₙ, bₙ) exceeds C log₂ aₙ for all n. For algorithms, the library gives fixed nondeterministic register programs over (ℕ, rem, eq0) with arbitrarily small logarithmic coefficients: for each ε > 0, one program with 3·2^p + 6 registers (any p > 3/ε) and no recursion stack has, on every input a ≥ b ≥ 1, a convergent computation returning gcd(a, b) with at most ε log₂ a + B remainder calls, and the same program written one function per line is a tail-recursive program with bounded stacks. These programs depend on ε, so the Main Conjecture for algorithms (deterministic or nondeterministic recursive programs) is not settled and remains open. Lower bounds are also formalized: every gcd certificate needs at least as many remainder facts as the shortest derivation, and the coprimeness complexity is at least (1 − ε) log₂ log₂ N on all but o(N²) coprime pairs below N.

records.title: Robust absorption for typed triangles
records.abstract: Typed triangle decomposition results from Paper II: a typical-host theorem under three-step links for four-label families; its nearly complete and balanced deductions with explicit type-weight hypotheses; a semidense two-label mixed-triangle theorem; a computer-assisted typical-host theorem for every admissible four-label family; and a terminal absorber obtained from a bounded signed certificate and explicit physical hinge supply. Divisibility includes global edge counts and local degree profiles. The typical-host hypotheses are retained; the result is not asserted for arbitrary divisible hosts. The repository contains the substantive proof development, including the finite family census and conserved-family constructions, with a small independent Mathlib-only Challenge.

records.title: Erdős Problem 1063: a lower bound for n_k and the structure of the exceptional index
records.abstract: For k ≥ 2 let n_k be the least n ≥ 2k such that n − i divides the binomial coefficient C(n, k) for all but exactly one 0 ≤ i < k (Erdős Problem 1063; Erdős and Selfridge 1983; OEIS A389360; Guy's Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, B31). Using the definition of n_k from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures verbatim, this project proves two results in Lean 4 with Mathlib. (1) For every k ≥ 2, n_k ≥ W'_k = ∏_{p^a ∥ k} p^(a + ⌊log_p(k − 1)⌋); the bound is attained in the sense that n_k − i₀ = W'_k for k = 4, 6, 14. (2) If n ≥ 2k, e < k, and every n − i with 0 ≤ i < k, i ≠ e, divides C(n, k), then e = n mod k and D(k, e) = ∏_{p^a ∥ k} p^(a + v_p(C(k − 1, e)) + ⌊log_p max(e, k − 1 − e)⌋) divides n − e. Result (2) was proved informally by the user rickyc in the erdosproblems.com discussion thread for the problem. It is the structural input of the exhaustive searches that extend the OEIS table (by jbell31 for 60 ≤ k ≤ 75, and by the author for k up to 140): an admissible n with exceptional index e must lie in the residue class e modulo D(k, e). This formalization makes the minimality of those computed values depend only on verified mathematics and on the search code; jbell31 had noted in the thread that a Lean proof of this divisibility would close that gap. formal-conjectures records upper bounds and small values of n_k but no general lower bound. The development also proves the Erdős–Selfridge observation and that Cambie's number k · lcm(1, …, k − 1) is admissible, so the lower bound holds for every k ≥ 2 without further assumptions.

records.title: An FPT Algorithm for Maximum-Weight Independent Set in Embedded Graphs, in Lean 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of a fixed-parameter theorem of "Maximum-weight independent set in embedded graphs parameterized by Euler genus and number of odd faces" (forthcoming), with a provably correct implementation of the algorithm as one fixed program for an explicit sixteen-register pointer machine. Lean proves that for every graph drawn in a closed surface of Euler genus gamma whose complement has k regions of odd total boundary length, and all integer vertex weights, the program outputs a maximum-weight independent set within 2^(c (p size(p) + 1)) (N size(M))^c bit operations, where p = gamma + k, N = |V| + |E| + 1, M = max(1, max |w_v|), size(x) is the binary length of x and c is an absolute constant; that is, 2^O(p log(p+1)) poly(N, log(M+1)) with an absolute polynomial exponent. Surfaces are represented by finite combinatorial flag maps; orientable and nonorientable surfaces, disconnected and noncellular drawings, loops, multiple edges, isolated vertices and negative weights are covered. The algorithm solves one exact linear program per retained component over a finite-group network whose size depends only on p, using exact integral quotient coordinates, midpoint convexity of class minima and a coarse Jensen inequality, and recovers an optimal set from perturbed edge costs. The cost is a logarithmic bit-cost measure including an explicit stack simulation of recursive calls. The proofs use exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Mader's theorem on highly connected subgraphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Mader's 1972 theorem in the form of Diestel's Theorem 1.4.3: for k ≥ 1, every nonempty finite simple graph with average degree at least 4k has a (k + 1)-connected induced subgraph H with e(H)/|H| > e(G)/|G| − k. Vertex connectivity is defined by deletion of fewer than k vertices (same definition as in the Menger–Hamiltonicity entry). Mathlib does not contain vertex connectivity or this theorem.

records.title: Spanning-Tree Maximization Forces Isoperimetry in the Square Lattice
records.abstract: Lean formalization of spanning-tree maximization over finite connected induced subgraphs of the square lattice. The development establishes edge isoperimetry of every maximizer, the maximum count and all maximizing lattice-isometry classes at every positive cardinality, and uniqueness of the canonical corner-strip domain for N >= 18. Nonuniqueness occurs exactly at N = 3, 8, 10, 13; the canonical count has exceptions at N = 7, 14, 17. It also establishes the sharp square-cardinality stability inequality, an exact scalar product formula and rational recurrence for corner-strip counts, the global extremal asymptotic expansion with O(N^(-1/2)) remainder, and the appendix's exact strip-energy Fourier identity, rectangular remainders, Green estimates, and explicit bounds.

records.title: Lavrentieff's Gδ homeomorphism extension theorem
records.abstract: Every homeomorphism between arbitrary subsets of completely metrizable spaces extends to a homeomorphism between Gδ supersets contained in the respective closures. Empty subsets and ambient spaces are included. A zero-oscillation construction first gives a Gδ continuous extension domain for maps to complete metric spaces. Restricting the two continuous extensions gives mutually inverse maps. The arbitrary supplied topologies are preserved by compatible complete metrics. Classical mathematics, with no mathematical novelty or priority claim.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Regular subgraphs of almost regular graphs (Alon–Friedland–Kalai)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Alon–Friedland–Kalai theorem for primes: for a prime p, every finite simple graph with maximum degree at most 2p − 1 and average degree greater than 2p − 2 contains a p-regular subgraph (a nonempty subgraph with all degrees 0 or p); as a corollary, every 4-regular graph plus an edge contains a 3-regular subgraph. The prime-power case of the paper is not stated. The proof uses Mathlib's Chevalley–Warning theorem.

records.title: Chang's version of Freiman's theorem and the Bogolyubov–Ruzsa lemma
records.abstract: Formalization of Chang's version of Freiman's theorem, with a 2-proper progression P: a finite set X of integers with |X + X| <= kappa |X| is contained in a 2-proper generalized arithmetic progression of dimension at most the Freiman dimension of X, hence at most 2 kappa - 1, with at most exp(10^32 kappa^7) |X| points. If kappa (2 kappa - 1) <= epsilon |X|, the dimension is at most floor(kappa - 1 + epsilon), as in Green and Tao. There is also a statement for subsets of ZMod q with q prime, where the progression has at most exp(10^30 kappa^7) |X| points. The bound on the size is weaker than that of Chang. The first step of the proof, the Bogolyubov-Ruzsa lemma, is stated too: if moreover |X| >= 7 * 10^7 kappa^2, then 2X - 2X contains a proper progression of dimension at most 3 * 10^5 kappa^2 with at least exp(-2 * 10^7 kappa^2) |X| points.

records.title: A smaller upper bound for superpermutations
records.abstract: For the shortest superpermutation length S(n), construct covering words with asymptotic bound S(n) <= n! + (n-1)! + (n-2)! + (926683/1814400 + o(1))(n-3)!. The development proves an explicit finite bound for every n >= 14 and its numerical consequences. The coefficient is approximately 0.510738. The argument combines a finite selection, a verified connector cover, and transport to larger alphabets.

records.title: Slow Equilibration and Persistent Stationary Correlations in Spherical Spin Glasses
records.abstract: Lean formalization of the six headline result groups: Theorem 1.2, Corollary 1.3, and Theorems 1.4–1.7. Theorem 1.2, Corollary 1.3, and the asymptotic clauses of Theorem 1.4 are conditional only on Chen’s finite-mixture Parisi formula. Universal pressure lower tails are proved internally. The finite-dimensional Haar comparison and Theorems 1.5–1.7 have no literature premise. The manuscript and exact model assumptions are included.

records.title: A proof of Kroó’s conjecture
records.abstract: For every origin-symmetric convex body with nonempty interior in a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, continuous real boundary functions admit uniform approximation by real homogeneous polynomials of consecutive degrees. The development proves all thirteen principal results of the cited manuscript, including parity approximation, dimension-only uniform approximation of the constant function, homogeneous Gaussian kernels with polynomially weighted errors, fixed-bandwidth one-sided weighted density, tensor density, Gaussian Fourier cutoff, convex weighted approximation, finite-family selection and positive spherical quadrature. The thirteen declarations and their conjunction are compared against an independent self-contained Challenge using only the standard three Lean axioms.

records.title: Chain returns and lower bounds for superpermutations
records.abstract: Prove explicit general lower bounds for the shortest superpermutation length S(n), valid for every n >= 8. The exact-order and quadratic-order formulas refine the lower-order terms while retaining leading correction (2+o(1))(n-4)! above n!+(n-1)!+(n-2)!. The development also proves asymptotic comparisons with earlier general formulas; the selected theorem statements specify their exact scope. Separate finite refinements prove S(10) >= 4033379 and S(14) >= 93891141150.

records.title: Proofs and corrections of OEIS conjectures
records.abstract: Machine-checked proofs of conjectures recorded in 29 entries of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS), together with corrections of the four conjectured statements that turn out to be false. Most of the sequences are coefficients of formal power series defined by functional equations, and most of the results describe their residues modulo small integers. The results form six families and a group of further results: the equation A(x*A - m*x*A^2) = x^2 (parity, residues modulo m^2, binary-digit divisibility and prime exponents for every m, with corrected residue classifications modulo 9 and 16 for A396843 and A396844); consecutive iterates F = x + F^{o r}*F^{o(r+1)} (every integer iterate modulo 2r, A396099, A396798, A396807); scaled inverses A(x - x*A(qx)/q) = x (every coefficient is 1 modulo q+1, and for even q the odd coefficients are exactly at the powers of 2, A393856-A393859); theta-series substitutions and theta-type sums (square patterns modulo 4, corrected for A380680, and a congruence modulo 16 for A355872); Catalan-type equations (residues modulo 2, 4 and 8 governed by powers of 2, A393172, A393171, A389536, A397588, A195194); equations with an exact halving step (residues modulo 4, 9 and 3, A389537, A389542, A389474, A389475); and further results on A396093, A392210, A396102 and its family F^{o r} = (1+x)*F^{o(r-1)}, A380056, A397346 and the greedy sequence A394576. Each family has its own Comparator configuration, and each OEIS entry has a self-contained paper in the repository.

records.title: Nearly linear directed cycles in vertex-transitive digraphs
records.abstract: Formalization of the near-linear directed-cycle theorem: for every real epsilon greater than zero, all sufficiently large finite connected vertex-transitive loopless digraphs on n vertices contain a simple directed cycle of length at least n^(1-epsilon). Connectedness means connectedness of the underlying undirected graph; cycles of length two are allowed. This is Theorem 1.5 of the archived revised manuscript by Bowen Li and Abhishek Methuku, with repaired arguments and replacement lemmas in its proof dependencies. It does not assert Hamiltonicity.

records.title: A density version of the binary Goldbach problem, after Alsetri and Shao
records.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no cited hypothesis, of Theorem 1.2 of A. Alsetri and X. Shao, Density versions of the binary Goldbach problem, arXiv 2405.18576v2, Acta Arith. 218, 2025, 285 to 295: if A is a set of primes whose relative lower density in every reduced residue class b mod W is at least some eta > 1/2, then almost all even positive integers are a sum of two primes from A. The entry also proves the paper's Theorem 1.1, that relative density 1 - epsilon in the primes alone does not suffice, and the sharpness of the constant 1/2 stated in its Remark 1.3. A derived result of this entry, not a result of the paper, shows that the hypothesis of Theorem 1.2 holds for the set of all primes, so the theorem is not vacuous. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; Theorem 1.2 concerns almost all even numbers. An AI agent wrote the Lean code, except the ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd code credited to its authors; the statements were checked against the paper by an AI agent and are offered for human audit.

records.title: The optimal Hessian bound for convex four-body central configurations
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 7.3 of arXiv:2609.35632 on the central configurations of the planar Newtonian four-body problem. At every strictly convex central configuration of four positive masses, the Hessian form Q of U + (λ/2)I is at least two thirds of its radial part K, and strictly so wherever K is positive. In the notation of the paper this is λ_max(G) < 1/3 for the explicit 2×2 matrix G of its Proposition 3.5, and by its Proposition 7.2 the constant 2/3 is optimal. It sharpens Theorem B of the paper, Q ≥ K/4. The definitions and the reduction to the normal form of Corbera, Cors and Roberts are those of the registered development lean4body-uniqueness. The new parts are a majorant that pays only the largest eigenvalue of S(y), an exact test that is positive definite exactly when λ_max(G) < 1/3, and a computer-assisted proof of that test: a branch and bound with interval arithmetic over the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations, reduced by a symmetry to half of it, and an exact Taylor-form theorem at the corner where the margin of the test vanishes. Lean's kernel checks the certificates with `decide +kernel`. The trusted base is Lean's kernel, including its built-in arithmetic on natural-number literals (GMP-accelerated), and the proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms.

records.title: Unique-Continuation-Planar
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of every theorem, lemma and proposition of "Unique continuation on planar graphs" (Bou-Rabee, Cooperman and Ganguly): a harmonic function on a periodic plane graph with periodic conductances that is bounded by one on a set of density at least 1 - epsilon is constant (Theorem 1.1), together with the exponential upper bound (Theorem 1.2), the zero case (Theorem 1.3), the topological lemma, the exponential lower bound of the appendix with its polynomial approximation lemma and three-ball proposition, and non-planar periodic conductances on Z^2 with a harmonic function supported on a diagonal (Theorem 5.1).  Three results the paper cites from the literature (Janiszewski's theorem at a point, unicoherence of the sphere and the discrete Moser estimate) are explicit hypotheses of the theorems that use them; the classical Liouville theorem for periodic networks and the discrete Remez inequality are proved. The four main theorems are independently checked using the UCPlanarAudit/ comparator pairs.

records.title: ORRW-Lower-Bound
